paper.title: The Max $K$-Armed Bandit: A PAC Lower Bound and tighter Algorithms

unmapped: Objective: return a sample whose reward is within epsilon of the overall maximal possible reward (max of support upper ends over arms) with probability > 1-delta; minimise expected number of samples ((epsilon,delta)-correct max-sample identification)
Rewards are real-valued with finite support maximum and tail condition P(X_k > mu*_k - eps) >= A eps^beta for 0 < eps <= eps_0 (Assumption 1)
The learner knows the tail-condition constants A, beta, eps_0
settings.definition_quote: There exist known constants $\CA>0$, $\beta\geq0$ and $\epsilon_{0}>0$ such that, for every $k\in K$ and $0<\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0}$, it holds that $$P\left(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{k}>\mu^{*}_{k}-\epsilon\right)\geq\CA\epsilon^{\beta}\,,$$ ... An algorithm is said to be \emph{$(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct} if $P\left(V>\maxmu-\epsilon\right)>1-\delta$. The expected number of samples $E[T]$ taken by the algorithm is the \emph{sample complexity}

settings.name_in_paper: Unified-arm model (arms mixed, sampled uniformly at random)
unmapped: The learner cannot choose arms: each sample comes from an arm chosen uniformly at random among K arms (single unified arm with mixture CDF F = (1/K) sum_k F_k)
Objective: return a sample within epsilon of the maximal possible reward with probability > 1-delta, minimising expected number of samples
Tail condition P(X_k > mu*_k - eps) >= A eps^beta for 0 < eps <= eps_0 (Assumption 1); learner knows A, beta
settings.definition_quote: In the unified-arm model, when the agent samples from this unified arm, a certain arm (among the multi arm) is chosen uniformly and a reward is sampled from this arm. We denote the CDF of the unified arm as $F(\mu)$, with $ F=\frac{1}{|K|} \sum_{k\in \KK} F_k $.

symbols.Delta_i: mu* - mu*_k: gap in maximal possible reward (support upper end) of arm k
symbols.sum_subopt: here: sum over all arms except one chosen optimal arm k* (other optimal arms included)

source.label: thm:lower:bound
source.quote: Suppose $\epsilon_{0}\leq\left(4\CA\right)^{-1/\beta}$, $\beta\leq1$ and let $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let $k^*$ denote some optimal arm, such that $\mu^{*}_{k^*} = \maxmu$. Then, under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, for every $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct algorithm, it holds that E[T]\geq \sum_{k\in \KK\setminus \{k^*\}}\frac{1}{8\CA\left(\min\left(\epsilon_{0},\epsilon+\maxmu-\mu^{*}_{k}\right)\right)^{\beta}}\ln\left(\frac{3}{16\delta}\right).

results.notes: Sum is over all arms except a single optimal arm k*; encoded with sum_subopt redefined in symbols. Gaps are in maximal rewards, not means.

symbols.Delta_i: mu* - mu*_k: gap in maximal possible reward of arm k

source.label: thm:alg1
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, for $\G\geq10$, Algorithm \ref{alg:example} is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct with a sample complexity of E[T]\leq \sum_{k\in\KK}\frac{\G-\ln(\delta)}{\CA \left(\max\left(\epsilon,\maxmu-\mu^{*}_{k}\right)\right)^{\beta}}+|\KK|N_{0}, where $N_{0}=\lfloor\frac{L-\ln(\delta)}{\CA\epsilon^{\beta}_{0}}\rfloor+1$ and $\G=6\ln\left(|\KK|\left(1+\frac{-\ln(\delta)}{\CA\epsilon^{\beta}}\right)\right)$

results.notes: Also (epsilon,delta)-correct. Corollary 1 states this matches Theorem 1 up to a log(K/epsilon) factor when more than one arm has mu*_k in [mu*-eps, mu*]; not recorded separately.

source.label: thm:lower:single
source.quote: Suppose $\epsilon_{0}\leq\left(\frac{|\KK|}{2\CA}\right)^{\frac{1}{\beta}}$, $\beta\leq1$ and let $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$, $\delta\in(0,1)$. Then, under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, for every $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct algorithm, it holds that E[T]\geq \frac{|\KK|}{4\CA\epsilon^{\beta}}\ln\left(\frac{3}{5\delta}\right).

results.notes: Unified-arm model; dependence labelled worst_case since it depends only on K, A, beta, epsilon, delta.

tuning: number of samples ceil(-ln(delta) K/(A eps^beta)) + 1

source.label: thm:alg:Single
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, Algorithm \ref{alg:example_S} is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct, with a sample complexity bound of E[T]\leq \frac{|\KK|\ln(\delta^{-1})}{\CA\epsilon^{\beta}}+2.

cited_results.cited_title: An asymptotically optimal algorithm for the max k-armed bandit problem
cited_results.setting_description: Max K-armed bandit, reward distributions in a specific family; sample complexity to find epsilon-close maximal sample w.p. 1-delta
